summary: Iter7 FRONTEND-only validation of TIMEUP batch: country-code dropdowns, referral, custom-room, bet input, KYC USDT, withdraw method, deposit warning, admin bulk actions, admin live custom-rooms table, room-list inflated counts, auto-refresh recharge, and Let-Win auto-stop. 12/13 flows PASS. Only failure is Let-Win auto-stop — after countdown the client never issues /games/fixed/stop, so user does NOT auto-win. Root cause is a stale-closure bug in GameHome.js (details in rca below). Everything else works end-to-end on the public preview URL at mobile viewport 420x860.

ui_bugs.issue: After clicking start-challenge-btn with force_win=true (auto_win returned true by /games/fixed/start), the client never calls /games/fixed/stop. Bet is deducted but the stopwatch never auto-stops and the user does not win. Observed 3 times: balance 500→480, no /games/fixed/stop request, no win-celebration, and the stale 'active' session subsequently blocks new starts with HTTP 409. Fix in GameHome.js line 62-72: the setTimeout(() => stop(), target*1000+50) captures a `stop` closure from the render where `phase` was still 'countdown'; inside stop() the guard `if (busy || phase !== 'running') return;` short-circuits. Use a ref for phase (phaseRef.current) or call stop via a functional pattern that reads latest state (e.g. store the auto-stop timer in a ref and let a phase-scoped effect trigger it, or read latest via useRef).

React hydration warning in console: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>'. Cause: option children include flag emoji + text with a className on <option> (styled span-like). Not visually broken but pollutes console and can cause SSR hydration mismatch. Consider using a custom shadcn Select or plain-text option content: <option>{`${c.flag} +${c.dial}`}</option> without className, or a proper Select/Combobox.

Because auto-stop is broken (above), the game_sessions doc stays status='active' forever, and future starts return 409 'You already have an active game session'. There is no client-side way to abandon/timeout the session. Backend should auto-expire sessions older than target+grace, or expose a POST /games/fixed/abort.

action_items: PRIMARY: Fix GameHome.js auto-stop stale closure. Minimal patch: keep phase in a ref (phaseRef) and check phaseRef.current inside stop(); OR clear the auto-stop by storing timer in a ref and firing stop via `stopRef.current()` where stopRef is updated every render. This unblocks the whole Let-Win feature.
Add a server-side sweeper or /games/fixed/abort to clear stale active sessions so users aren't permanently blocked with 409.
Fix <option> hydration warning in Register.js & Login.js (remove className on <option> or switch to shadcn Select).

OPTIONAL: When the Guide onboarding overlay is active, hide/defer the fixed-position 'REFER' and 'Play with Friends' controls so the first tap after login doesn't fall on a covered element (referral modal intermittently ignores the first click on a fresh session).
critical_code_review_comments: GameHome.js line 67 uses a captured `stop` closure with stale `phase` — classic bug. Refactor to phaseRef + a wrapper `doStop()` that reads phaseRef.current, OR skip the guard for the auto-triggered path.
Backend fixed_start has no timeout for stale 'active' sessions; combined with above, users get soft-locked.

Countries dropdown uses value=dial only — India(+91) and Canada(+1)/US(+1) share dial '1' so selecting 'Canada' is indistinguishable from 'United States' in the current select_option by value. Consider using country code as value and mapping to dial internally.

The 'REFER' badge is fixed at bottom-[132px] right-4 z-40 and 'Play with Friends' bar is fixed bottom-[70px] z-40 — both live on the same z layer and overlap on smaller viewports (~<380 wide). Consider raising REFER by ~14px or repositioning.
get_current_user backfill of referral_code confirmed working (TU966782 rendered for a fresh user).
Console shows 1 hydration warning per <select> render — investigate for SSR compatibility.

rca of the issue: Let-Win auto-stop bug: In /app/frontend/src/pages/GameHome.js, the useEffect at line 62-72 handles the 3-2-1 countdown. When count reaches 0, it does: setPhase('running'); setTimeout(() => swRef.current?.start(), 50); if (autoWinRef.current) setTimeout(() => stop(), target*1000+50);  — the arrow function passed to setTimeout captures the CURRENT-render's `stop` function via lexical closure. That `stop` was created in a render where `phase === 'countdown'` (React has not yet re-rendered with the new phase='running' state at the moment useEffect body executes). When the 5-second timer fires, it invokes that captured stop(), which contains the guard `if (busy || phase !== 'running') return;` — with the captured `phase === 'countdown'`, the guard short-circuits and stop() returns without calling /games/fixed/stop. Bet stays deducted; the DB session remains status='active' forever; subsequent start attempts return 409. Reproduction: (a) admin sets force_win on user, (b) user starts fixed challenge, (c) observe /games/fixed/start 200 + auto_win:true but no /games/fixed/stop after target+delay. Mitigation: (i) use a phaseRef updated in a useEffect on `phase` change and check phaseRef.current instead of phase inside stop(); (ii) OR store the auto-stop timer id in a ref and, in a new effect that fires when phase becomes 'running', schedule the timer there so the closure captures the correct phase; (iii) OR skip the guard when triggered via auto-win path (call an internal doStop() directly). Any of these fixes will resolve. Also add backend cleanup for stale active sessions (e.g. mark as expired if server_start + target + 10s < now).
